sections.heading: Verifying a valid probability density function

questions.q: A continuous random variable $X$ has probability density function $f(x)=\dfrac{1}{4}$ for $0\leq x\leq4$, and $f(x)=0$ otherwise. Verify that this is a valid pdf.
questions.answer: Since $f(x)=\dfrac{1}{4}\geq0$ throughout, and $\int_0^4\dfrac{1}{4}\,dx=\dfrac{1}{4}(4)=1$, the total area under $f$ equals $1$, confirming a valid pdf (the uniform distribution on $[0,4]$).

questions.q: Determine the value of $c$ such that $f(x)=c$ for $2\leq x\leq6$, and $f(x)=0$ otherwise, is a valid pdf.

sections.heading: Finding an unknown constant in a pdf

questions.q: A continuous random variable $X$ has pdf $f(x)=kx$ for $0\leq x\leq5$, and $f(x)=0$ otherwise. Find $k$.
A continuous random variable $X$ has pdf $f(x)=k(4-x)$ for $0\leq x\leq4$, and $f(x)=0$ otherwise. Find $k$.
A continuous random variable $X$ has pdf $f(x)=kx^2$ for $0\leq x\leq3$, and $f(x)=0$ otherwise. Find $k$.

sections.heading: Finding probabilities by integrating the pdf

questions.q: Using $f(x)=\dfrac{2}{25}x$ for $0\leq x\leq5$, find $P(X\leq2)$.
Using the same pdf, find $P(2\leq X\leq4)$.
Using $f(x)=\dfrac{1}{8}(4-x)$ for $0\leq x\leq4$, find $P(X\geq2)$.
Using $f(x)=\dfrac{1}{9}x^2$ for $0\leq x\leq3$, find $P(X\leq1)$.
For the pdf $f(x)=\dfrac{2}{25}x$ on $0\leq x\leq5$, find the cumulative distribution function $F(x)$.
Using $F(x)=\dfrac{x^2}{25}$, find $P(X\leq3)$ and hence $P(X>3)$.
For the pdf $f(x)=\dfrac{1}{8}(4-x)$ on $0\leq x\leq4$, find the cumulative distribution function $F(x)$.
questions.answer: $F(x)=\int_0^x\dfrac{1}{8}(4-t)\,dt=\dfrac{1}{8}\left(4x-\dfrac{x^2}{2}\right)=\dfrac{x}{2}-\dfrac{x^2}{16}$. Checking $F(4)=2-1=1$ confirms the total probability is correctly $1$.

questions.q: For the pdf $f(x)=\dfrac{1}{9}x^2$ on $0\leq x\leq3$, find the cumulative distribution function $F(x)$.

sections.heading: Using the cdf to find probabilities

questions.q: Given $F(x)=\dfrac{x^2}{25}$ for $0\leq x\leq5$, find $P(1\leq X\leq4)$.
Using $F(x)=\dfrac{x}{2}-\dfrac{x^2}{16}$, find $P(1\leq X\leq3)$.
Using $F(x)=\dfrac{x^3}{27}$ for $0\leq x\leq3$, find $P(1\leq X\leq2)$.

sections.heading: Expectation of a continuous random variable

questions.q: Using $f(x)=\dfrac{2}{25}x$ for $0\leq x\leq5$, find $E(X)$, using $E(X)=\int xf(x)\,dx$.
Using the uniform pdf $f(x)=\dfrac{1}{4}$ for $0\leq x\leq4$, find $E(X)$, and verify it matches the midpoint of the interval.
questions.answer: $E(X)=\int_0^4x\cdot\dfrac{1}{4}\,dx=\dfrac{1}{4}\left[\dfrac{x^2}{2}\right]_0^4=\dfrac{1}{4}(8)=2$, matching the midpoint of $[0,4]$, as expected for a uniform distribution.

questions.q: Using $f(x)=\dfrac{1}{9}x^2$ on $[0,3]$, find $E(X)$.

sections.heading: Variance of a continuous random variable

questions.q: Using $f(x)=\dfrac{2}{25}x$ on $[0,5]$ and $E(X)=\dfrac{10}{3}$ (found earlier), find $\text{Var}(X)$, using $\text{Var}(X)=E(X^2)-\left[E(X)\right]^2$.
Using the uniform pdf $f(x)=\dfrac{1}{4}$ on $[0,4]$ and $E(X)=2$ (found earlier), find $\text{Var}(X)$.
Using $f(x)=\dfrac{1}{9}x^2$ on $[0,3]$ and $E(X)=\dfrac{9}{4}$ (found earlier), find $\text{Var}(X)$.
Using the cdf $F(x)=\dfrac{x^2}{25}$ for $0\leq x\leq5$, find the median $m$ of $X$, solving $F(m)=0.5$.
Using the same cdf, find the lower quartile $Q_1$, solving $F(Q_1)=0.25$.
Using $F(x)=\dfrac{x}{2}-\dfrac{x^2}{16}$ for $0\leq x\leq4$, find the upper quartile $Q_3$, solving $F(Q_3)=0.75$.
questions.answer: $\dfrac{x}{2}-\dfrac{x^2}{16}=0.75$. Multiplying by $16$: $8x-x^2=12\Rightarrow x^2-8x+12=0\Rightarrow(x-2)(x-6)=0$. Since the domain is $[0,4]$, $x=6$ is rejected, so $Q_3=2$.

questions.q: Using the cdf $F(x)=\dfrac{x^3}{27}$ for $0\leq x\leq3$, find the median $m$ of $X$, to three decimal places.

sections.heading: A well-designed word problem: waiting time at a bus stop

questions.q: This question has four parts. The waiting time $X$ (minutes) for a bus is modeled by $f(x)=\dfrac{3}{64}x^2$ for $0\leq x\leq4$, and $f(x)=0$ otherwise. (a) Verify this is a valid pdf. (b) Find the cdf $F(x)$, and use it to find the probability a passenger waits more than $3$ minutes. (c) Find $E(X)$, the mean waiting time. (d) Find the median waiting time, to three decimal places.
questions.answer: (a) $\int_0^4\dfrac{3}{64}x^2\,dx=\dfrac{3}{64}\left[\dfrac{x^3}{3}\right]_0^4=\dfrac{3}{64}\cdot\dfrac{64}{3}=1$, and $f(x)\geq0$ throughout, confirming a valid pdf. (b) $F(x)=\int_0^x\dfrac{3}{64}t^2\,dt=\dfrac{x^3}{64}$. $P(X>3)=1-F(3)=1-\dfrac{27}{64}=\dfrac{37}{64}\approx0.578$. (c) $E(X)=\int_0^4x\cdot\dfrac{3}{64}x^2\,dx=\dfrac{3}{64}\left[\dfrac{x^4}{4}\right]_0^4=\dfrac{3}{64}(64)=3$ minutes. (d) Solving $F(m)=0.5$: $\dfrac{m^3}{64}=0.5\Rightarrow m^3=32\Rightarrow m=32^{1/3}\approx3.175$ minutes.
